See also: Gallo, gallò, Gallo-, and gallo-

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Breton gall (“a Gaul or a foreigner”), from being a language found in eastern Brittany of the non-Celts, from Latin gallus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɡa.lo/
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Homophones: galop, galops (except regionally)

Noun

[edit]

gallo m (uncountable)

  1. Gallo

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Catalan: galó
  • → English: Gallo
  • → German: Gallo
  • → Spanish: galó

Further reading

[edit]
  • “gallo”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Galician

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • galho (reintegrationist)

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /ˈɡaɟo/ [ˈɡɑ.ɟʊ]
  • IPA(key): (standard) /ˈɡaɟo/ [ˈɡɑ.ɟʊ]
  • IPA(key): (gheada) /ˈħaɟo/ [ˈħɑ.ɟʊ]

  • Rhymes: -aɟo
  • Hyphenation: ga‧llo

Etymology 1

[edit]

Probably from Vulgar Latin *galleus, from Latin galla (“oak-apple”).[1] Cognate with Portuguese galho.

Noun

[edit]

gallo m (plural gallos)

  1. fork; bifurcation
  2. prong
  3. forked branch
  4. (tools) fork
Derived terms
[edit]
  • co gallo de
  • esgallar
  • gallado
  • gallar
  • galleiro
  • galleta
  • galleto

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

gallo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of gallar

References

[edit]
  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “gallo”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “gallo”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “gallo (galla)”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “gallo”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN
  1. ^ Coromines, Joan; Pascual, José Antonio (1983–1991), “gajo”, in Diccionario crítico etimológico castellano e hispánico [Critical Castilian and Hispanic etymological dictionary]‎[1] (in Spanish), Madrid: Gredos

Further reading

[edit]
  • “gallo”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026

Etymology 1

[edit]
Etymology tree

Proto-Italic *galsos
Latin gallus
Italian gallo

    Inherited from Latin gallus, from Proto-Italic *galsos, from Proto-Indo-European *gelH- (“to call”).

    gallo m (plural galli, feminine gallina)

    1. rooster, cock

    • gallo cedrone
    Related terms

    • galletto
    • gallicinio
    • galliformi
    • gallina

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    From Latin Gallus (“Gaul; Gallic”).

    Noun

    [edit]

    gallo m (plural galli, feminine galla)

    1. Gaul (native or inhabitant of Gaul) (usually male)

    Adjective

    [edit]

    gallo (feminine galla, masculine plural galli, feminine plural galle)

    1. Gallic
      Synonym: gallico

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • Gallia
    • gallico

    Etymology 3

    [edit]

    Verb

    gallo

    1. first-person singular present indicative of gallare

    Spanish

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]
    Etymology tree
    Proto-Indo-European *gelH-
    Proto-Italic *galsos
    Latin gallus
    Spanish gallo

      Inherited from Latin gallus, from Proto-Italic *galsos, from Proto-Indo-European *gelH- (“to call”).

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
       
      • IPA(key): /ˈɡaʝo/ [ˈɡa.ʝo]
      • IPA(key): /ˈɡaʝo/ [ˈɡa.ʝo] (Equatorial Guinea, most of Latin America and Spain)
      • IPA(key): /ˈɡaʎo/ [ˈɡa.ʎo] (Andes Mountains, rustic northern Spain, Paraguay, Philippines)
      • IPA(key): /ˈɡaʃo/ [ˈɡa.ʃo] (Buenos Aires and environs)
      • IPA(key): /ˈɡaʒo/ [ˈɡa.ʒo] (elsewhere in Argentina and Uruguay)

      • Audio (Colombia):(file)
       
      • Rhymes: -aʝo
      • Rhymes: -aʝo (Equatorial Guinea, most of Latin America and Spain)
      • Rhymes: -aʎo (Andes Mountains, rustic northern Spain, Paraguay, Philippines)
      • Rhymes: -aʃo (Buenos Aires and environs)
      • Rhymes: -aʒo (elsewhere in Argentina and Uruguay)

      • Syllabification: ga‧llo

      Noun

      [edit]

      gallo m (plural gallos, feminine gallina, feminine plural gallinas)

      1. rooster, cock (male domestic chicken)

      Noun

      [edit]

      gallo m (plural gallos)

      1. megrim (genus Lepidorhombus, a kind of fish)
      2. John Dory (edible marine fish; Zeus faber or Zeus ocellata)
      3. common poppy (Papaver rhoeas)
      4. corn tortilla sandwich, usually filled with meat and/or beans, and other ingredients
      5. (boxing) bantamweight (weight class ranging from 112 to 118 pounds)
      6. voice crack (sudden, unintentional change in register, especially during puberty or while singing)
      7. (Mexico) serenade (love song sung directly to one's love interest)
        Synonym: serenata
      8. (architecture) ridge beam
        Synonyms: hilera, cumbrera, parhilera

      Noun

      [edit]

      gallo m (plural gallos, feminine galla, feminine plural gallas) (colloquial)

      1. (Chile) guy, dude
        Synonyms: tipo; see also Thesaurus:tío
        Conocí a ese gallo anoche en el teatro.
        I met that guy last night at the theatre.
      2. (Venezuela) nerd
        Synonyms: friki, empollón

      • rabos de gallo

      • riña de gallos

      Related terms

      Descendants
